title: Add rate-normalized canary detector with degradation profiles and staged rollback hooks
author: Priya Nambiar
release_notes: Introduces a rate-normalized canary detector and degradation profile primitives. Enables safer staged rollbacks based on combined latency and throughput regressions; configurable defaults are non-breaking and behind the perf-canary feature flag.
description: Motivation: existing canary detectors were sensitive to transient spikes when request rates differed significantly between control and candidate; this led to noisy alerts during A/B traffic shifts. This PR introduces a rate-normalized detector that weights latency/throughput signals by per-window QPS and explicit degradation profiles to better surface true regressions. What changed: 1) a new detector implementation (canary/detectors/rate_normalized_detector.py) that computes rate-weighted deltas for P50/P95 and request success-rate, 2) a degradation profile DSL (canary/profiles/) to encode multi-metric degradation patterns (e.g., latency-only, throughput-degen, combined), 3) staged rollback hooks and an operator-facing config (console: Rollout -> Canary -> Detector) to tune sensitivity and rollback granularity, 4) end-to-end integration tests and a synthetic traffic harness for CI. How it works: the detector computes per-bin metrics for control and candidate, scales the contribution of each bin by observed QPS and a configurable smoothing window, then applies profile-defined thresholds across metrics and a composite score with hysteresis to avoid flip-flop. If composite score crosses the profile's failure threshold for N consecutive windows the rollout guard transitions to 'soft-fail' and can optionally trigger staged rollback hooks (candidate->10%->0%). Config and rollout: new config keys under perf_canary.detectors.rate_normalized: window_seconds, smoothing_alpha, min_qps_per_bin, profile_name, consecutive_windows, rollback_strategy (none|soft|hard), staged_weights (comma-separated list). Default settings are conservative to avoid surprising behavior. Testing: we added a synthetic harness that replays production-like QPS patterns to validate noise resistance and a small collection of historical regressions to assert detection and rollback behavior. Docs and migration: console docs updated with examples and recommended defaults; feature is behind perf-canary.rate-normalized feature flag and does not change existing detectors unless explicitly enabled. Rollout plan: merge to main can be toggled for internal Canary experiments; monitor for two weeks with dashboards perf/canary/rate-normalized and a rollback cooldown. Related work: ENG-1987 (canary false positives investigation), ENG-2041 (staged rollback automation).

tests_summary: Unit coverage added for detector thresholds and profile parsing; integration synthetic harness validated that detector suppresses false positives during QPS shifts in 8/10 replay scenarios; two historical regressions triggered correct staged rollback in tests. CI originally failed on arm timing flakiness and was fixed by adjusting replayer sleeps.
deploy_notes: Feature gated behind perf-canary.rate-normalized. Recommended conservative defaults: window_seconds=60, smoothing_alpha=0.2, min_qps_per_bin=5, consecutive_windows=3, rollback_strategy=soft, staged_weights=50,20,0. Monitor dashboards perf/canary/rate-normalized and perf/rollouts/* for composite_score and rollback transitions. Staged rollback hooks call the rollout orchestration API with configured weights and include a cooldown of 600s between stages.
